tasks.short: Assess physical security threats and the scope of the problem.

steps.what: Show stored incident counts by place, not by person
Assess the nature and level of physical security threats
State the scope once that threat is determined

outputs: filed copy of signed threat assessment v1

tasks.design: A dashboard in {BI} shows stored incident counts by place and does not name a person or produce a score. The specialist assesses the nature and level of the physical security threats and determines the scope of the problem. They sign the assessment. A job files that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: A score could be treated as the threat decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored incident rows can be counted by place.
tasks.still_hard: What the threat is, and how wide the problem is, is still a judgement on the site.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist determines the scope and signs it.

ambition.what: Refresh the place counts when a new incident is stored, and sign a new assessment.

tasks.altitude: The assessment stays. Copying the counts shrinks.

reach.learn: That a count is not a score

evidence.claim: The operations digest says reports and records can be a dashboard on the existing records.
Digest [S21] says a score a decision-maker draws strongly on counts as the decision, so this design produces no threat score and no score of a person.
Digest [S20] bars a solely automated decision with significant effect, so a finding about a person stays with the specialist.
Digest [S23] says works-council consent is required before staff monitoring, so this design does not add a view of named staff.

unknowns: Which incidents are in the count.
Who else must accept the scope.
research_questions: How often a stored incident has no place.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the assessment is the site judgement, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the specialist still walks the site. The high end assumes only the place counts are no longer added by hand. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Respond to emergency situations while on call.

steps.what: Respond to emergency situations on an on-call basis
Sign the emergency note after the response

outputs: filed copy of signed emergency note v1

tasks.design: Responding to emergency situations, on call, stays with the specialist. A job files the note in {DOCS} only after the response, and only after the specialist signs it. The job does not answer the emergency.
tasks.previous_blocker: A workflow could delay the response until a form was complete.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed note can be filed after the specialist is back.
tasks.still_hard: The response depends on what is happening at the site.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist responds, then signs the note.
tasks.altitude: The response stays. Filing the signed note shrinks.

reach.task: Read the note only after the response
reach.learn: That the file is not the response

evidence.claim: Digest [S20] bars a solely automated decision with significant effect, so a finding about a person stays with the specialist.

assumptions: The job does not dispatch or decide the response.
unknowns: Which emergencies the specialist must attend in person.
research_questions: How often the first call is a false alarm.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the response is the response itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes every emergency is still attended by the specialist. The high end assumes only the signed note is no longer rewritten. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend improvements in security systems or procedures.

outputs: filed copy of signed recommendation v1

tasks.design: Recommending improvements in security systems or procedures stays with the specialist. A job files the recommendation in {DOCS} only after they sign it. The job does not change a system.
tasks.previous_blocker: A generated list could be treated as the improvement to make.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed recommendation can be filed for the client.
tasks.still_hard: What is worth changing is still a judgement.

ambition.what: File a recommendation the same week a test fails, and only the signed version.

tasks.altitude: The recommendation stays. Filing the signed text shrinks.

reach.task: Act only on the signed recommendation

evidence.claim: The operations digest says a draft must work from approved sources, and a named person signs.

assumptions: The job does not recommend or implement.
research_questions: How often a procedure and a system change must move together.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the recommendation is the judgement itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes every recommendation is still written by the specialist. The high end assumes only the signed copy is no longer retyped. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform risk analyses and develop countermeasures.

steps.what: Perform risk analyses of the site

outputs: filed copy of signed risk analysis v1

tasks.design: Performing the risk analysis and developing appropriate countermeasures stays with the specialist. A job files the analysis in {DOCS} only after they sign it. There is no risk score, and the job does not put a countermeasure into service.
tasks.previous_blocker: A score could stand in for the analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed analysis can be filed on the existing record.
tasks.still_hard: Which countermeasure fits this site is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist performs the analysis and signs the countermeasures.
tasks.altitude: The analysis stays. Filing the signed analysis shrinks.

evidence.claim: Digest [S21] says a score a decision-maker draws strongly on counts as the decision, so this design produces no threat score and no score of a person.
Digest [S20] bars a solely automated decision with significant effect, so a finding about a person stays with the specialist.

assumptions: Nothing goes live before a separate signed instruction.
unknowns: Which risks the client wants analysed.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time on the analysis is the judgement itself, already the person's work.

incremental.description: Update the stored standard list or the drawing index when it changes, and clear drafts the specialist rejects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the analysis is still done on the site. The high end assumes only the signed analysis is no longer copied. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The security specialist spends the week on the site, the incident, and the decision. Filing a signed note can move. No model scores a person, watches staff, or changes a live security system.
reach: A client sees only the criteria or the finding the specialist signed.
A supervisor gets an emergency note after the specialist has already responded.
skills_to_grow: Tell a stored incident count from a threat decision.
Refuse a view that scores or tracks named staff.
role.ambitious_version: A signed test or a signed recommendation can be filed the same day, and the specialist still decides it.
